correctness.rationale: The foot of the common center on each facet plane is strictly inside that face: for another outward normal the dot product at the foot is strictly below h. These feet are the face circumcenters, all with circumradius √(1−h²), so all faces are acute. The two face angles opposite any edge agree by the sine rule on acute angles. The four face angle-sum equations then equate angles on opposite edges, hence also opposite lengths. The three acute triangle half-edge lengths determine positive box-axis squares by complementary sums, yielding a congruent alternating-corner realization centered at the origin. There a²+b²+c²=1, h⁻²=a⁻²+b⁻²+c⁻²≥9, and the center box has axes h/(a√(1−h²)), etc., centroid zero and squared radius L²=1+ρ². Opposite edges give half-lengths d_i, all strictly less than one because each a_i²<1 and h>0. For a triple missing index i, substituting p_i=ρu_i gives |p_i−c_j|²=1 and p_i·(c_j−p_i)=0 for all j in the triple. This is its planar circumcenter; the face is acute since the sum of any two squared half-edges minus the third is twice a positive center-box axis square. The positive barycentric average of the three squared distances is then 1+|x−p_i|², proving their first intersection at radius 1 and uniqueness there. The equal-weight four-center identity gives first fourfold intersection at L. Before radius 1 the graph's cycle spaces inject under inclusions; separate opposite matchings successively merge two and then one component and give H₁ gains of one and two, with gains combined at tied thresholds. The tetrahedron boundary at 1 kills H₁ and creates H₂, and the tetrahedron at L kills it. The natural finite closed-convex nerve theorem transfers this persistence to offsets. Alexander duality for the compact union with homotopy type S² gives two complement components in the compactification, exactly one bounded in R³. In the five-ball nerve for q<ρ no central ball meets any singleton triple and there are no 3-simplices; the tetrahedron-boundary 2-cycle cannot bound. At and above ρ every proper outer subfamily meets the core, and the nerve is exactly the cone on that boundary. Finally the barcode recovers the three d_i including multiplicities, and then L²=S/2 and the complementary center-box axis squares L²−d_i², giving the displayed original semiaxes and critical core radius. These arguments cover the regular case, tied scales and closed-ball equality cases over all stated coefficient fields.
residual_risks: The inverse result is internal to the normalized concentric disphenoid family. The proof does not classify general four-site clouds or a ball of freely varying center.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The sphere containment bounds the central complementary component inside the ρ-ball, and tangency already yields interior uncovered points arbitrarily close to that radius. This is substantial prior information about the radial size of the gap (and yields a bounded complementary region for smaller cores); it alone is not a claim of a unique void or contractibility after filling. The reviewed calculation uses acute-face geometry to identify triple intersections as singletons, combines them with all edge and fourfold thresholds, tracks inclusion maps, and recovers the semiaxes from the resulting interval data. The nerve and algebra steps after the thresholds are routine and are credited as such.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the complete offset barcode, including exact incidence thresholds and their persistence pairings, the topology of the varying centered core including contractibility, and congruence recovery within this family. Nour already gives the same arrangement, contacts and coverage of the central sphere at radius ρ, as well as a different sharp origin-containing inscribed-ball result. Those prior facts imply substantial metric information about the central gap and are not themselves new; the reviewed claim resolves the full topology and inverse data. The other inspected catalogue works treat volume or optimal inscribed balls, not the resolved filtration.
residual_risks: The Katsuura original and older disphenoid work (including the Leech citation in the earlier volume record) were not directly inspected. The cited nonprimary Disphenoid page could not be retrieved and is not used as evidence of no coverage.

value.rationale: The four outer unit balls come from a specific published geometric counterexample, so analyzing their full scale-dependent homotopy and the role of its central ball is motivated, rather than a generic persistence exercise on arbitrary four points. The proof gives explicit multiplicities and ties, shows why the gap persists until the central contacts enter the nerve, and then proves contractibility, not just coverage of a particular sphere. More unusually, the full offset barcode recovers the original tetrahedron within a nontrivial family. This makes the interval data an exact inverse invariant and determines the critical core radius from the earlier edge scales. The worthwhile contribution is this classification and reconstruction, not the elementary nerve theorem or the prior inscribed-ball calculation.
residual_risks: Value is a particular solved geometric family with fixed normalization and origin-centered core, not an unrestricted inverse-persistence result.
